SIG_3G_ALIGNMENT.question: is first-valid age p or p+1?
SIG_3G_ALIGNMENT.finding: it consumes ema50.shift(1) — the PREVIOUS bar EMA50, which is VALID only when that bar had age >= 50
SIG_3G_ALIGNMENT.correction: the EMA50 dependency class is right but the temporal alignment is period + 1. A p-not-p+1 implementation would emit one spuriously valid row per segment.

COOLDOWN_STATE_CONTRACT.source: indicators.apply_cooldown: last = -(n+1); if arr[i]: if i-last<n: arr[i]=False else: last=i
COOLDOWN_STATE_CONTRACT.state: last — index of the last ACCEPTED fire
COOLDOWN_STATE_CONTRACT.OUTPUT_vs_STATE: non-fire bar: output trivially False, last carries unchanged. Fire bar: output depends on incoming last; if REJECTED, last stays unknown, so ambiguity PROPAGATES rather than resolving.
COOLDOWN_STATE_CONTRACT.why_a_simple_n_bar_rule_is_wrong: an ambiguous fire at segment position q can push the determinism point to q+n. There is no fixed warmup that is safe in general.
COOLDOWN_STATE_CONTRACT.sufficient_condition_identified: if NO raw fire occurs in the first n-1 bars of a segment, the first fire at position p >= n-1 is accepted for every admissible incoming last (since i-last <= p+1), and it sets last deterministically
COOLDOWN_STATE_CONTRACT.REQUIRED_IMPLEMENTATION: forward-propagate the SET of admissible last values from segment start; a fire bar is AVAILABLE_VALID only when every admissible value yields the same accept/reject decision
COOLDOWN_STATE_CONTRACT.status: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — this is the last place where INIT/UNKNOWN could silently become FALSE
